gaps.explanation: Statement total 8,505,027 is the GAAP (accrual) proprietary statement, Exhibit H Totals 2025 column (p10): total operating revenues 7,937,728 + non-operating miscellaneous 6,131 + interest income 244,727 + intergovernmental transfer 275,370 + ARPA grant revenue 41,071 = 8,505,027. The business-type detail lines are Schedule 20 'Statement of Cash Receipts and Cash Disbursements Compared to Budget', Actual Budgetary Basis column (p24, cash basis): Electric 1,904,462 + Water 475,356 (printed 555,650 less transfers from other funds 80,294) + Sewer 391,305 (printed 1,112,164 less transfers 720,859) + Care Center (June 30) 5,646,964 = 8,418,087. Gap 86,940 is the cash-vs-accrual difference (receivable changes, consumer deposits, etc.); no line is missing or duplicated. (The per-department accrual columns on p9-10 - Electric 1,789,677+91,573, Water 431,711+5,246, Sewage 384,055+7,692, Care Center 5,332,285+6,131+140,216+275,370+41,071 - tie to 8,505,027 if the user ever prefers them to Schedule 20.)

Statement total 7,664,654 is Exhibit H Totals 2025 total operating expenses (p10, accrual; includes depreciation and amortization 362,957, excludes principal and capital purchases). Detail is Schedule 20 Actual Budgetary Basis cash disbursements (p24): Electric 1,843,174 + Water 387,280 (printed 513,228 less transfers to other funds 125,948) + Sewer 859,150 (printed 989,848 less transfers 130,698) + Care Center (June 30) 5,437,967 = 8,527,571. Schedule is 862,917 above the statement because cash disbursements include capital and debt payments and exclude depreciation; both totals are printed correctly on their own basis. (The p9-10 department columns Electric 1,518,651 + Water 297,304 + Sewage 264,399 + Care Center 5,584,300 = 7,664,654 would tie exactly.)
